title: Can Large-Customer Gains Remain a Key Driver of NET's Revenue Growth?
detail:
Can Large-Customer Gains Remain a Key Driver of NET's Revenue Growth?
Om Jaiswal
Thu, September 10, 2026 at 10:15 AM EDT 3 min read
NET
ZS
PANW
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Cloudflare NET is seeing strong momentum among its largest customers, which is driving strong revenue growth and customer retention. In the second quarter of 2026, the company ended with 4,698 customers generating more than $100,000 in annual revenues, up 27% year over year. Cloudflare added 282 large customers during the second quarter and a record 986 net additions in large customers, year over year. Each large-customer group, from $100,000 to more than $5 million in annual revenues, posted record year-over-year net additions in the second quarter of 2026.

Large customers are also becoming a bigger part of Cloudflare's business. They accounted for 73% of total revenues in the second quarter, up from 71% a year ago. Strong expansion among these customers helped push dollar-based net retention to 120%, up from 118% in the previous quarter and 114% a year ago. This shows that existing customers are increasing their spending on Cloudflare's products, while the company continues to add new large accounts.

The strong performance of large customers is supporting Cloudflare's overall financial growth. Second-quarter revenues increased 36% year over year to $696.1 million. Management said new customer bookings grew at their fastest rate in more than five years, while pipeline generation increased at its fastest sequential pace in five years. Cloudflare added more than 80,000 paying customers during the second quarter, resulting in 74% year-over-year growth in its paying customer base.

The company is also seeing customers adopt multiple products, including its developer platform, Zero Trust and application security offerings. Some customers also replaced several legacy tools with Cloudflare's broader platform, giving the company more opportunities to increase spending within existing accounts. Overall, continued growth in large customers, higher spending from existing accounts and stronger adoption across Cloudflare's product portfolio could help support the company's revenue growth in the near term.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Cloudflare's 2026 and 2027 revenues indicates year-over-year growth of 31.1% and 28.2%, respectively.

Cloudflare Faces Tough Competition

Cloudflare is seeing strong growth in large customers, but competitors Zscaler ZS and Palo Alto Networks PANW are also expanding their enterprise businesses.

Zscaler ended fiscal 2026 with 4,182 customers generating more than $100,000 in annual recurring revenue (ARR), up 20% year over year. The company also had 785 customers with more than $1 million in ARR, up 18%. Its Z-Flex offering is helping customers expand their spending, with Z-Flex generating more than $770 million in total contract value in the fourth quarter, up more than 60% sequentially.

title: Cloudflare (NET) Soars 10.5% on Upbeat Outlook, Says Opportunities ‘Larger’ Than Business
detail:
Cloudflare (NET) Soars 10.5% on Upbeat Outlook, Says Opportunities ‘Larger’ Than Business
Angelica Ballesteros
Wed, September 9, 2026 at 10:00 PM EDT 2 min read
NET
Trade NET on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Cloudflare Inc. (NYSE:NET) grew its share price by 10.51 percent on Wednesday to finish at $10.51 apiece after issuing a highly optimistic outlook, saying that its future opportunity "could be much larger" than its business.

Speaking at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026, Chief Finance Officer Thomas Seifert said that Cloudflare Inc. (NYSE:NET) is now moving beyond a traditional software-as-a-service (SaaS) model to becoming an agentic AI platform amid the rapidly growing artificial intelligence sector.

It highlighted huge opportunities in several areas, including inference, content protection, and payments infrastructure.

In this light, the company raised its north star outlook to 50 percent annually from 40 percent at present, while revenues are projected to grow by 36 percent year-on-year.

Photo by George Morina on Pexels

Q2 Revenues Up 36%

In the second quarter of the year, Cloudflare Inc. (NYSE:NET) said that it grew its revenues by 36 percent to $696.1 million from $512 million in the same period last year.

Net loss, however, widened by 237 percent to $169.98 million from $50.4 million year-on-year, amid a 206 percent higher operating loss.

OpenAI Partnership

Earlier this month, Cloudflare Inc. (NYSE:NET) joined forces with OpenAI for the early launch of Vulnerability Discovery and Remediation, which could help organizations pinpoint high-risk vulnerabilities and automatically block attacks at the edge before they can be exploited.

With the service, eligible customers are able to triage what is actively under fire, buy time with instant edge protection, and ship verified fixes faster.

The service is available in early access through Cloudflare Managed Defense.

"If your security team is manually fighting AI-driven attacks, you're not just burning them out—you're losing. Now, we're shifting the defense strategy away from chasing patches one vulnerability at a time to an automated approach," Cloudflare Inc. (NYSE:NET) CEO Matthew Prince said.

Hedge Funds Bullish

Partnership aside, institutional investors appeared to have been bullish about their long-term growth prospects for the company in the second quarter of the year.

During the period, 87 hedge funds held positions in the stock, up from 84 in the quarter previously.

More notably, their combined holdings soared by 11.8 percent to $3.97 billion from $3.55 billion.

While we acknowledge the potential of NET as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. title: Why Cloudflare Rallied Today
detail:
Why Cloudflare Rallied Today
Billy Duberstein, The Motley Fool

NVDA

Trading disclosure

Shares of Cloudflare (NYSE: NET) rallied on Wednesday, up 10.5% on the trading day.

While Cloudflare didn't report any company-specific news today, investors may be appreciating it as an ancillary beneficiary of Meta Platforms' (NASDAQ: META) new Muse AI agent.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Muse was introduced late yesterday, and Meta stock is rallying today. However, Cloudflare rallied even more, as it provides low-latency, distributed, secure computing infrastructure and should therefore be an ancillary beneficiary, as it will handle increased edge computing demand from personalized consumer agents going forward.

Cloudflare operates the "pipes" for edge AI

Cloudflare's distributed infrastructure helps consumers route, secure, and optimize web traffic. As such, anything that drives increased web traffic or places a premium on enhancing security for that traffic will benefit Cloudflare.

Yesterday, Meta unveiled Muse, a personalized agent that can securely execute tasks for consumers. It was a big unveiling, with CEO Mark Zuckerberg taking to social media to emphasize Meta's security safeguards around personal data when using the new personal agent.

Meta has been spending massive amounts on artificial intelligence infrastructure lately, and Muse is its first major AI-first product, aside from the AI improvements to Meta's core Facebook and Instagram social media platforms.

Meta's social media platforms have an enormous 3.6 billion daily active users. Needless to say, if even a small portion of those users begin using highly personalized Muse agents to execute day-to-day tasks across the web, that should greatly increase web traffic. That means more and more business for Cloudflare.

Cloudflare had already partnered with Meta on AI as far back as 2025, when Meta deployed its Llama open-source model across Cloudflare's Workers AI platform, which enables local inference for AI developers. Last quarter, Cloudflare's CEO, Matthew Prince, noted that, for the first time in its history, over 50% of the traffic on Cloudflare's network was non-human, agentic traffic. Cloudflare also recently announced Wallet, which enables trusted and secure commerce transactions between agents and merchants. It appears Muse will likely make extensive use of these capabilities.

Shopify (SHOP) stock opened higher on Wednesday after the e-commerce firm said it has acquired Tailwind Labs, the company behind the widely used Tailwind CSS. The announcement is significant for SHOP, given that Tailwind CSS is installed more than 110 million times per week and is used by prominent names like ChatGPT, Cloudflare (NET), Reddit (RDDT), and X.

That said, Shopify shares have reversed their intraday gains in recent hours and are now headed to end the Sept. 9 session down more than 5%.

What the Tailwind Labs Acquisition Means for SHOP Shares

In its press release, Shopify confirmed that Tailwind CSS will remain open source and MIT-licensed, and its existing team will continue to maintain the framework.

SHOP stock pushed higher initially because the acquisition could strengthen the firm's storefront, checkout, and broader developer ecosystem.

Tailwind is already a significant part of Shopify's tech stack as it positions itself around agentic commerce and artificial intelligence (AI) driven shopping experiences.

However, investors shouldn't expect this deal to directly boost SHOP's earnings or revenue.

Piper Sandler Raises Price Target on Shopify Stock

Also on Wednesday, Piper Sandler issued a bullish note in favor of Shopify shares, raising its price target to $180, which signals potential upside of more than 40% from here.

The investment firm expects SHOP to grow revenue by 32% year-on-year to $19.5 billion in 2027, and expand its free cash flow margins by about 170 basis points annually over the next three years.

Importantly, Piper Sander analysts believe the firm's existing merchant base will contribute more to its future growth than net-new merchants.

On the flip side, however, Shopify has a history of losing about 1.5% on average in September and another 1.37% in October — a seasonal pattern that dulls its near-term appeal.

Shopify Remains Buy-Rated Among Wall Street Firms

Investors should note that Piper Sandler is not alone in recommending owning SHOP shares at the current price.

According to Barchart, the consensus rating on Shopify sits at "Strong Buy," with the mean price target of about $175 indicating it could rally significantly through the remainder of 2026.

Cloudflare (NET) Shares Skyrocket, What You Need To Know
What Happened?

Shares of cloud security and performance company Cloudflare (NYSE:NET) jumped 10.1% in the afternoon session after the company introduced a new AI security service integrating OpenAI's cyber models with its infrastructure, fueling a sustained rally in its stock price. 

According to company announcements and industry reports, Cloudflare shares have climbed steadily since the September 3rd launch of "Vulnerability Discovery and Remediation," a new capability within its Managed Defense service. The offering leverages the OpenAI Daybreak Defense Network, specifically utilizing the highly advanced GPT-5.6 Cyber model, to automatically find, validate, and suggest fixes for software vulnerabilities. By combining deep codebase investigation with real-time traffic data from Cloudflare's global network, the service can deploy custom web application firewall (WAF) rules to block attacks at the edge while simultaneously drafting code patches for developers to review. 

The market's growing enthusiasm around this strategic integration with OpenAI's frontier models is further supported by the company's robust underlying financial performance. During its recent second quarter, Cloudflare reported revenue of $696.1 million, up 35.9% year-over-year, alongside an adjusted EPS beat of $0.29. Top-line momentum was underscored by billings growth of 34.8% to $753.5 million, though GAAP operating margins were pressured by a one-time impairment charge. Bolstered by this fundamental strength and the rapid rollout of new AI-driven cybersecurity tools, management confidently lifted both its full-year revenue and adjusted EPS guidance, giving investors further conviction in the company's long-term growth trajectory.

Is now the time to buy Cloudflare? Access our full analysis report here, it's free.

What Is The Market Telling Us

Cloudflare's shares are extremely volatile and have had 35 moves greater than 5% over the last year. But moves this big are rare even for Cloudflare and indicate this news significantly impacted the market's perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 6 days ago when the stock gained 3.1% on the news that software equities broadly gained momentum following a pullback in treasury yields and second-quarter financial results from Snowflake. Lower Treasury yields supported the move after Fed Governor Christopher Waller signaled support for keeping rates steady. The 10-year yield fell to 4.756%, while the 2-year yield declined to 4.328%, according to CNBC.Because software valuations are heavily based on cash flows expected years into the future, lower yields reduce the discount rate applied to those earnings and can increase the value investors assign to the group today.Snowflake surged after reporting earnings and increasing its forward outlook, sparking widespread optimism across the enterprise software industry. Taking a closer look at the quarter, SNOW's revenue reached $1.55 billion, up 35% year on year, driven by product revenue of $1.48 billion, which grew 37%, the company reported in an official press release. The upbeat report bolstered investor sentiment regarding enterprise tech demand and software spending.
